patient_population: People whose CFTR genotype produces little or no modulator-responsive protein including many nonsense and rare variants
prevalence_or_population: CFF 2024: approximately 92% eligible for at least one modulator after Alyftrek; 2434 ineligible by age or genotype; 1226 ineligible adolescents/adults with data. FACT from CFF ADR 2024.
clinical_burden: Residual classic CF pathophysiology in those without a protein-targeted option. INTERPRETATION pending trial and outcomes analysis.
economic_burden: Not quantified from public claims data in MVP. Use utilization proxies only when cited.
treatment_gap: No approved mutation-agnostic CFTR restoration therapy as of the therapy table in this repo.
pipeline_density: To be measured from reviewed programs and trials in Phase 4.
evidence_strength: High for US prevalence from CFF; preclinical/clinical tractability is a separate question.
notes: Keep mRNA gene replacement gene editing and readthrough as sub-mechanisms until classification is reviewed. Do not treat ineligible count as a TAM.

subcategory: Eligible but not prescribed or intolerant
patient_population: People eligible for a modulator who are not prescribed one including tolerability and access issues
prevalence_or_population: CFF: 623 people aged 12+ in 2020 with no CFTRm prescription in 2022-2024 versus 12975 with ivacaftor or ETI in all years 2020-2024.
clinical_burden: Mixed. CFF notes milder sweat chloride and lower care utilization in the unprescribed group so this is not equivalent to the ineligible population.
economic_burden: Insurance and specialty-pharmacy friction are hypothesized; not measured in patient-level public data.
treatment_gap: Next-generation modulators with better tolerability or care-delivery interventions could be relevant. HYPOTHESIS not fact.
evidence_strength: Moderate. Reasons for non-prescription are heterogeneous.
notes: Do not collapse this group into N1.

subcategory: Residual lung disease exacerbations inflammation structural damage
patient_population: People on highly effective modulators who still have lung function impairment exacerbations or advanced lung disease
prevalence_or_population: Mean FEV1 89.1% predicted in 2024 among ages >7; IV-treated PEx 12.1% versus 31.5% in 2019. Residual disease is smaller than pre-HEMT but not zero.
clinical_burden: Exacerbations hospitalizations and advanced lung disease remain clinically important for a subset. FACT: PEx and transplant volumes fell; FACT: they did not reach zero (61 lung transplants in 2024).
economic_burden: PEx treatment days among those with at least one PEx remained 14 median days in 2024.
treatment_gap: Airway clearance anti-inflammatories and antimicrobials remain widely used. Whether residual disease is a distinct drug opportunity is an analytical question for Phase 4-7.
pipeline_density: CFF pipeline shows substantial anti-inflammatory and mucociliary programs including discontinued assets. Treat density as unreviewed until Phase 4.
evidence_strength: High for residual utilization; interpretation of venture attractiveness is later.
notes: Do not read mean FEV1 89% as absence of a pulmonary problem.

patient_population: People with persistent airway infection especially Pseudomonas MRSA and nontuberculous mycobacteria
prevalence_or_population: PA 23.3% of cultured in 2024 down from 52.0% in 2009; MRSA 13.1%; NTM 11.6% of those with a mycobacterial culture. Among ages 60+ NTM 18.7% and PA 41.8%.
clinical_burden: Chronic infection remains associated with lung disease. Measurement is sensitive to fewer cultures since 2020.
economic_burden: Inhaled antibiotic use remains common among PA-positive patients (tobramycin 51.2% aztreonam 30.3%).
treatment_gap: Existing inhaled antibiotics and azithromycin; emerging phage and novel antimicrobials on the CFF pipeline page.
pipeline_density: To be measured after excluding discontinued programs.
evidence_strength: High for prevalence; moderate for whether public data can separate chronic versus intermittent infection.
notes: CFF explicitly warns that fewer visits affect microbiology ascertainment.

patient_population: Adolescents and adults with CFRD or impaired glucose tolerance
prevalence_or_population: CFRD 19.2% overall in the complications population (4.2% age<18 29.3% adults; n=32492 excluding transplant). HbA1c reported for 5019 people with CFRD. CGM use ~58% among those with diabetes.
clinical_burden: CFF: CFRD is associated with weight loss lung-function decline and increased mortality. Insulin remains guideline standard of care.
economic_burden: Not a public CF-specific claims total. Chronic insulin and CGM imply ongoing resource use.
treatment_gap: Insulin is SoC; 16.4% of people with CFRD had no treatment noted; non-insulin therapies 8.0%. No CF-specific disease-modifying metabolic drug is in the approved-therapy table.
pipeline_density: CFF Nutritional-GI pipeline includes a bionic pancreas program; CF-specific CFRD drug pipeline appears thinner than CFTR restoration. Confirm in Phase 4.
evidence_strength: High for prevalence and SoC; low-to-moderate for CF-specific product opportunity until pipeline review.
notes: Complications exclude transplant recipients so post-transplant diabetes is understated.

patient_population: People with pancreatic insufficiency and people with CF-related liver disease
prevalence_or_population: PERT 80.2% in 2024. Cirrhosis 2.7% and non-cirrhotic liver disease 3.5% in complications population. 861 people with cirrhosis. UDCA prescribed in 10.1%.
clinical_burden: Malabsorption remains common. Advanced CFLD is smaller but severe (portal hypertension markers among cirrhosis: esophageal varices 25.0%).
economic_burden: PERT and supplements are chronic. Advanced CFLD care and transplant are high-intensity. No public cost build in MVP.
treatment_gap: PERT products exist; CFF recommends against routine UDCA to prevent advanced CFLD. No approved disease-modifying CFLD therapy in the MVP therapy table.
pipeline_density: Nutritional-GI programs listed on CFF pipeline including lipase alternatives. Density unreviewed.
evidence_strength: High for PERT use; moderate for CFLD addressable population and endpoints.
notes: Older adults have lower PERT use which CFF interprets as milder surviving phenotypes not solved pancreatic disease.

patient_population: Adults especially ages 40 and older including a growing 60+ group
prevalence_or_population: Adults 61.6% of the 2024 Registry. Ages 40-49 n=3248; 50-59 n=1598; 60+ n=1437. Median predicted survival 65.4 years.
clinical_burden: New 2024 chapter reports cancer BP and lipids. Adult anxiety 31.9% depression 30.2% osteopenia 19.4% osteoporosis 8.3% sinus disease 50.2% hypertension 8.7%. FEV1 in 40+ is ~70-73% predicted — lower than the all-age mean.
economic_burden: Aging-related care is likely health-system intensive. Not a quantified market in public data.
treatment_gap: This may be a care-delivery and screening problem more than a CF-specific newco. HYPOTHESIS to pressure-test. Do not assume venture attractiveness.
pipeline_density: Likely sparse CF-specific drug pipeline. Confirm in Phase 4.
evidence_strength: High for demographics; emerging for cancer/CVD detail; low for a default biotech thesis.
notes: Included because the Registry now documents the shift not because it is a presumed company-formation opportunity.

patient_population: People with CF managing chronic multi-drug regimens especially adults
prevalence_or_population: Mean 3.0 clinic visits in 2024 down from 4.3 in 2019. Dornase 80.6% hypertonic saline 62.6% among ages >=6. 60.4% seen by a pharmacist. Adult-majority population.
clinical_burden: Time on inhaled therapies and care coordination remain burdens after modulators. Public Registry does not publish minutes-per-day of treatment.
economic_burden: Specialty pharmacy and visit volume are visible only as utilization proxies.
treatment_gap: Digital monitoring adherence support adult-care capacity and exacerbation prediction are possible solution classes not yet ranked.
pipeline_density: Interventional CT.gov set will include behavioral and device studies; classify in Phase 4.
evidence_strength: Moderate. Burden is widely described; quantified time-use is mostly literature not Registry.
notes: Allows healthcare-services theses beside therapeutics. Do not force a drug score onto a services problem.
